title: The City agreed to buy two buildings from an owner with City orders and unpaid-bill liens

beats.text: San Francisco agreed to buy two buildings on Laguna Street, both from the same owner.

visual.label: 624 and 601-617 Laguna Street
visual.sub: two buildings, one seller: Pacifica SFO LLC

beats.text: The price for the pair: 24,810,000 dollars.

visual.label: dollars: the two purchase prices approved by the Board

beats.text: Yet the City’s own departments had recorded orders and unpaid-bill liens against that seller.

b: orders and liens against the seller

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The owner, Pacifica SFO LLC, took both parcels in December 2016.

visual.fromLab: notice of default against Pacific Institute
visual.toLab: both parcels deeded to Pacifica SFO LLC

beats.text: The Board approved 624 Laguna Street in July 2024,
for 13,780,000 dollars.
And 601-617 Laguna Street in July 2025, for 11,030,000.
Both are assisted-living buildings for Public Health, bought with Proposition C money.

visual.title: For the Department of Public Health

beats.text: The Board’s analyst reported an appraisal supporting each price.

visual.line: affirmed that the proposed purchase price of $13,780,000 was fair market value

beats.text: A letter of intent between the City and the seller dates from May 2022.

visual.fromLab: letter of intent, City and seller

beats.text: The first lead: what the City already had on record against the seller.

visual.label: Before the vote
visual.sub: what the City’s own departments had recorded

beats.text: At 601-617 Laguna: three health liens,

visual.title: 601-617 Laguna Street
visual.sub: recorded in the five years before the vote

beats.text: three Building Inspection orders, four water liens.

visual.title: 601-617 Laguna Street
visual.sub: recorded in the five years before the vote

beats.text: So what did the City know of the buildings’ condition? And did the price account for it?

visual.line: What the City knew of the buildings’ condition, and whether the price took account of it

beats.text: Liens like these are routine. Every health lien was released, but the three orders show no revocation.

visual.label: Every health lien released
visual.sub: the three orders of abatement show no revocation

beats.text: The second lead: 624 Laguna closed 24 days after its vote.

visual.label: 624 Laguna Street
visual.sub: deed to the City 24 days after the vote

beats.text: 601-617 Laguna has no deed yet: under the signed agreement,

visual.toLab: no deed or notice of completion on the index

beats.text: title passes only after the repairs.

visual.toLab: no deed or notice of completion on the index

beats.text: Yet the City’s tables show 20,000,000 dollars paid to the title company.

visual.label: paid to Stewart Title Guaranty Co, fiscal 2026

beats.text: At the first closing, 10,000,000 dollars of the price goes to the seller, before the work is done.

beats.text: The third lead: in 2025 the City’s water utility recorded five liens against the seller.

visual.label: water liens against the seller, 2025
visual.sub: four before the vote, one after; each released

beats.text: Four before the vote, one after. Each was released by January 2026.

visual.label: water liens against the seller, 2025
visual.sub: four before the vote, one after; each released

beats.text: The fourth lead: that 20,000,000 is one total. 11,030,000 buys the building.

visual.title: Board file 250704: $20,000,000 in all
rows: Paid to the seller for repairs, up to

beats.text: Up to 8,140,000 more pays the seller to repair it, without competitive bidding.

visual.title: Board file 250704: $20,000,000 in all
rows: Paid to the seller for repairs, up to

beats.text: The fifth lead: the agreement was signed in August 2025, before the ordinance took effect on 4 September.
That voucher date is an update stamp, not a payment; the escrow receipt would settle it.

visual.text: $20,000,000 to the title company: the date is the system’s update stamp, not a stated payment date

beats.text: The records don’t show whether the appraisals took account of the orders, or whether they were cured.

cards: Whether the appraisals took account of the orders of abatement
Whether the orders were cured, or their cost taken off the price

beats.text: What would settle it? The escrow and disbursement records, and Building Inspection’s records.

cards.what: The escrow and disbursement records at Stewart Title for contract 1000036698
Building Inspection complaint and abatement records for both parcels

beats.text: Orders and liens like these are routine, and mostly released. Nothing here alleges misconduct.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
